Name: Crantzer
Question: Would Count Dooku and Asajj Ventress defeat Emperor Palpatine together in a fight when Darth Maul and Savage Oppress could not?
Answer: Contrary to popular belief, I’d say yes. Dooku is criminally underrated in his skill and Force power. He has been shown to take on two of the most powerful Jedi effortlessly on numerous occasions. He also managed to go toe-to-toe with Yoda (the second most powerful Force user in history). Ventress was no slouch, either. In fact, she was so powerful that Palpatine sensed her powers were too strong for Dooku to have as an apprentice. So, he made Dooku get rid of her. Had she progressed in Dooku’s training for a few more years, I do believe they’d be a good match against the powerful Sith Lord.

Question: Why does Thanos never touch the Time Stone in Infinity War?
Answer: All throughout the MCU, no one has ever touched the Time Stone (though other Infinity Stones have been touched). Notice how they’re some sort of barrier around it every time someone has the Time Stone in their hand: The Time Stone differs from the other stones in the sense that unlike all the others (reality, mind, power, space, and soul), time cannot be touched and/or felt. Thus, the Time Stone has a sort of barrier around it when a living person touches it. However, a simple inanimate object/machine has no problem touching it.

Question: Excluding Thanos, which Marvel film had the most universe threatening villain?
Answer: Actually, Thanos is nowhere near the most powerful MCU villain. That would be this guy: Dormammu, Destroyer of Worlds Dormammu is literally a multiversal threat and consumer of worlds. His power was so great that even mystic beings like the Ancient One couldn’t stand a chance against him. In fact, the combined power of all mystic arts can’t even kill him — the best they can do is prevent him from destroying everything. Petty, tiny beings like Thanos would be no problem for him. Some other honorable mentions (all of which are more powerful than the Mad Titan) include: Ego, Surtur, Hela, and of course Kang.

Question: Why did Black Panther call Bucky the “White Wolf” in Avengers: Infinity War?
Answer: It was a reference to the comics. In comics, the White Wolf is a completely different person. His name is Hunter. He and his family had crash-landed in Wakanda, so King T’Chaka decided to adopt and train him. Thus, Hunter is T’Challa’s brother. Hunter eventually became a warrior (like the Black Panther), completely loyal to Wakanda. The MCU likes to change up things from comics or cartoons, so it’s likely that Bucky is just their version of the White Wolf. And with this, it’s plausible that we’ll see this mantle of White Wolf used in the future for Bucky to serve the people of Wakanda in their time of need, for everything they’d done for him.

Question: Who would win in a fight, Hela or Ultron?
Answer: Physically, Hela would win. Her power is above that of gods, and was even too much for the Allfather himself to contain. Her necroswords can also cut Uru. So yes, she’d be able to cut through and/or destroy the android. However, the problem is that Ultron transcends the physical realm. See, the whole reason Ultron was so dangerous in Age of Ultron was because he managed to infiltrate the internet. It’s what gave him the ability to remotely control the entire world. Even if Hela destroyed his body, she couldn’t destroy Ultron’s essence. He would simply sit in the internet until he made a new body. Perhaps he’d even learn from his mistakes and make a more powerful one as time progressed.
